title: Add ChatGPT project sync and backfill project assignments
description:
## Summary

Add full ChatGPT project sync so Quaid can pull projects, preserve project membership for conversations, and backfill already-synced conversations with project assignments. Today the codebase has partial project-related scaffolding but the pull path does not organize ChatGPT chats under projects or backfill existing records.

## Scope

- Fetch ChatGPT projects and project metadata.
- Pull project conversations and preserve `project_id` / `project_name` on synced records.
- Backfill previously synced ChatGPT conversations and assign them to the correct projects where possible.
- Update storage, exports, and docs if project metadata becomes part of the public contract.

## Success Criteria

- ChatGPT sync pulls project containers and project-associated conversations.
- Synced ChatGPT conversations persist project metadata consistently across SQLite and Parquet storage.
- Existing local ChatGPT conversations can be backfilled and assigned to projects without requiring a destructive reimport.
- Docs and exports describe the new project-aware behavior clearly.

title: Remediate CLI, runtime, and documentation consistency audit
description:
## Summary

Consolidate the current inconsistency audit into tracked remediation work across the CLI, runtime behavior, and docs. The main goal is to make the public contract of `quaid` match what the code actually does, and to remove or fix user-visible mismatches that make the project harder to trust or operate.

This epic covers the findings from the repository audit:

1. ChatGPT incremental sync uses `create_time` instead of remote update time.
2. Semantic search is documented as real ONNX `multilingual-e5-small`, but the implementation is still mock-based.
3. `quaid list --archived` exists in the CLI but is ignored by the implementation.
4. `README.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md` drift from the real storage paths, auth storage, model layout, and pipeline behavior.
5. Several user-facing command hints print invalid command syntax.
6. Markdown export treats multi-conversation output paths as directories in a surprising way.
7. Search output prints a generic `score` even though semantic mode returns distance and hybrid mode returns an RRF score.

## Scope

- Capture the audit as individually actionable child issues.
- Fix code paths that are clearly wrong or misleading.
- Update docs where the implementation is already correct but the written contract is stale.
- Leave larger roadmap work, such as full ChatGPT project sync and backfill, to a separate follow-up epic.

## Success Criteria

- Each audit finding is represented by a child issue with enough context to execute independently later.
- The CLI help, runtime guidance strings, and README examples use the same command syntax.
- Unsupported flags are removed or implemented; they are not left as misleading no-ops.
- Architecture and README docs describe the actual storage layout, auth storage mechanism, and pipeline behavior.
- Export and search UX mismatches are fixed so users do not get misleading output or path behavior.
- A separate follow-up epic exists for ChatGPT project sync and project backfill work.

title: Align semantic-search contract with the current embeddings backend
description:
## Summary

Resolve the mismatch between the semantic-search contract and the current embeddings implementation. The repo currently documents ONNX-backed `multilingual-e5-small` embeddings and model download behavior, while the implementation still uses deterministic mock embeddings.

Relevant code paths:

- `quaid-core/src/embeddings/model.rs`
- `src/commands/search.rs`
- `README.md`
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`

## Proposed Change

- Decide on the near-term contract: either implement the real ONNX/runtime path or explicitly document the mock/dev status.
- Remove any user-facing messages that claim `quaid pull` downloads the model unless that behavior is actually implemented.
- Make the README and architecture docs match the true runtime behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The semantic-search implementation and the docs describe the same backend behavior.
- User-facing CLI messages no longer promise model download behavior that does not exist.
- README and architecture docs are internally consistent about embeddings and model files.

title: Fix ChatGPT incremental sync to honor remote update timestamps
description:
## Summary

Fix ChatGPT incremental sync so `--new-only` uses the remote update timestamp instead of falling back to conversation creation time. The current behavior can skip updated conversations after the first sync, which breaks the advertised incremental-sync contract.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Sync a ChatGPT conversation locally.
2. Update that same conversation remotely so the server-side `update_time` changes.
3. Run `quaid pull --new-only` or `quaid chatgpt pull --new-only`.
4. Observe that the conversation can be skipped because the list mapping currently uses `create_time` as `updated_at`.

Relevant code paths:

- `quaid-core/src/providers/chatgpt/types.rs`
- `quaid-core/src/providers/chatgpt/mod.rs`
- `src/commands/pull.rs`

## Proposed Change

- Use `update_time` from ChatGPT conversation list items when available.
- Fall back to `create_time` only when the remote payload truly lacks an update timestamp.
- Add or update tests around incremental skip decisions so the bug does not regress.

## Acceptance Criteria

- ChatGPT conversation list parsing preserves remote update timestamps.
- `quaid pull --new-only` and `quaid chatgpt pull --new-only` do not skip updated ChatGPT conversations incorrectly.
- Tests cover the timestamp mapping and the skip behavior.

title: Remove unsupported --archived flag from quaid list
description:
## Summary

Remove the unsupported `--archived` flag from `quaid list`. The CLI advertises the flag, but the handler ignores it and the storage query does not filter archived conversations, which makes the flag a misleading no-op.

Relevant code paths:

- `src/main.rs`
- `src/commands/list.rs`

## Proposed Change

- Remove the `--archived` flag from the public CLI surface.
- Remove any dead parameter plumbing tied to the flag.
- Update command help text and docs if they mention archive filtering.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `quaid list --help` no longer exposes `--archived`.
- The list command implementation no longer carries unused archive-filter plumbing.
- There are no stale docs or examples referencing `--archived`.

title: Update README and architecture docs to match the runtime behavior
description:
## Summary

Update `README.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md` so they describe the actual storage layout, credential storage, model-file layout, and pipeline behavior. The current docs still describe paths and behaviors that no longer match the runtime implementation.

Relevant docs and code paths:

- `README.md`
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `src/main.rs`
- `src/commands/pull.rs`
- `quaid-core/src/credentials.rs`
- `quaid-core/src/pipeline/stages.rs`
- `quaid-core/src/storage/traits.rs`
- `quaid-core/src/embeddings/model.rs`

## Proposed Change

- Align default data-directory documentation with the real runtime default.
- Document that provider credentials live in the system keyring, not in SQLite.
- Fix attachment/media path documentation to match the current implementation.
- Fix model-file layout documentation to match the current implementation, or update the implementation if another issue changes the contract.
- Update pipeline docs anywhere they still claim attachment downloads happen inside the media stage when they do not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- README and architecture docs no longer describe stale storage paths or stale auth-storage behavior.
- Attachment, model, and pipeline descriptions match the actual codebase.
- The docs are reviewed for consistency with the current CLI API and runtime output.

title: Fix user-facing command hints to use the real provider-first CLI syntax
description:
## Summary

Fix user-facing command hints so they use the actual provider-first CLI syntax. Several runtime messages currently suggest invalid commands like `quaid auth chatgpt` or `quaid pull chatgpt`, even though the real CLI shape is `quaid chatgpt auth` and `quaid chatgpt pull`.

Relevant code paths:

- `src/commands/auth.rs`
- `src/commands/pull.rs`
- `src/commands/list.rs`
- `src/commands/export.rs`
- `src/main.rs`

## Proposed Change

- Audit every runtime guidance string that instructs the user to authenticate or sync.
- Update them to match the actual Clap command tree.
- Verify the command examples in docs and help output remain consistent with the runtime hints.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Runtime guidance strings use valid provider-first command syntax.
- Auth, pull, list, and export messages no longer suggest invalid commands.
- CLI examples in docs and help text match the same syntax.

title: Fix markdown export path semantics for multi-conversation output
description:
## Summary

Fix markdown export path semantics so the output path behaves predictably. Right now, multi-conversation markdown export turns the provided `<PATH>` into a directory, which is surprising when the user passes something that looks like a file name such as `notes.md`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Sync or otherwise store multiple conversations locally.
2. Run markdown export with a file-looking path such as `quaid export notes.md --format markdown`.
3. Observe that the command can create a directory named `notes.md/` and write multiple files underneath it.

Relevant code paths:

- `src/main.rs`
- `src/commands/export.rs`

## Proposed Change

- Decide on a clear contract for markdown export when multiple conversations are selected.
- Either require a directory path explicitly or derive a sibling directory name in a deterministic way.
- Update help text and docs so the contract is obvious before the command runs.
- Add tests for single-conversation and multi-conversation markdown export behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Multi-conversation markdown export has a predictable, documented path contract.
- Passing a file-looking path does not silently create a misleading directory layout.
- Tests cover both single-file and multi-file markdown export cases.

title: Fix search result metric labeling across semantic and hybrid modes
description:
## Summary

Fix search result labeling so the CLI does not print a generic `score` for metrics that mean different things. Semantic search currently returns L2 distance, while hybrid search returns an RRF-style higher-is-better score, but both are printed under the same label.

Relevant code paths:

- `quaid-core/src/storage/duckdb.rs`
- `src/commands/search.rs`
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`

## Proposed Change

- Decide on a user-facing presentation for semantic and hybrid ranking metrics.
- Rename the displayed metric, normalize it, or hide it where it would be misleading.
- Update docs/examples so search output terminology matches the chosen contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Search output no longer presents incomparable ranking metrics under the same `score` label.
- Semantic mode and hybrid mode use clear, accurate output terminology.
- Any docs that describe search ranking are updated to match the implementation.
